name: Elkanah
overview: Elkanah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Korah. Notably, he was spared from death during the rebellion, distinguishing him within his lineage. His heritage connects him to a significant Levitical family line, emphasizing his role within the covenant community.
namesAndTitles: The name Elkanah means 'G-d [El] has possessed,' reflecting a recognition of divine ownership or blessing. This proper name, as recorded in Exodus 6:24, carries no indication of being divinely given but holds theological significance in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elkanah as the son of Korah, establishing a direct paternal link. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented within the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Elkanah's significance lies in his survival from the rebellion, a fate that befell many in his family line, highlighting God's preservation of certain individuals within a rebellious generation. His connection to Korah situates him within a notable Levitical lineage, underscoring the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant people despite challenges. This preservation serves as a testament to God's sovereignty and mercy.
